conviction_note: The evidence points both ways and nets to about zero. On the positive side, the CFO said on 2026-09-15 that the Q3 margin was running better than guided, and the Fed hike plus strong industry loan growth support the NII line. On the negative side, the 10-year yield rose 85bp in Q3 against $250bn of AFS securities in a Category I bank, so CET1 likely sits at or below the bottom of the 10-10.5% target and buybacks probably slow. The industry's IB fees were also soft. The name has sold three straight EPS beats on NII and margin. So p_up is 50 on an abs_move of 4.5, giving a scaled number of 0 against an impact_sum of +0.05. The two measurements agree that there is no edge here.
bar: Q3 2026 EPS $1.85 (Zacks, revised up marginally in the week before the print, via the Zacks 'Oct. 13 before market open' coverage; Hudson Labs consensus table also $1.85, https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/wells-fargo-q3-2026-earnings-preview-wfc-results-preview). Revenue $22.15bn (Zacks) to $22.34bn (Hudson Labs). Company guide is FY26 NII ~$50bn +/- (ex-markets ~$48bn) and FY expense ~$55.7bn, reiterated 2026-09-15 (https://www.kitco.com/news/off-the-wire/2026-09-15/wells-fargo-cfo-sees-stronger-2026-loan-growth-healthy-us-economy). No sourced Q3 NII consensus found. Two estimate sources agree on EPS, so sizes are not capped for the bar.
positioning_check: Short interest was 24.5m shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, 0.8% of shares outstanding, 1.72 days to cover (sweep row, equibles.com/stocks/wfc/shortinterest, read 2026-10-12). This is not a crowded short. Baseline 25-delta skew is +0.63 vol points (near neutral), put/call OI 0.63, and the priced lean is 'balanced'. The event-implied move is 3.93%, and the 4-print median reaction is 5.16% with 3 of 4 down. Run-up is -5.77% over 20 days and +2.64% over 5 days, -13.3% from the 52-week high. TIKR reports WFC fell 8.4% from the 2026-09-16 Fed hike to 09-24 against about 4% for XLF.

findings.finding: At the Barclays conference on 2026-09-15, the CFO said Q3 net interest margin would be better than the bank's initial expectation, against a July guide of 'modest compression, roughly in line with Q2's -4bp'. He held FY26 NII at ~$50bn and said loan growth would beat the mid-single-digit guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NII/NIM is the line this stock trades on. Q2 2026 beat EPS ($2.00 vs ~$1.72) and fell 2.71% because the FY NII guide was held and Q3 NIM compression was guided (https://www.fxleaders.com/news/2026/07/15/wfc-stock-slips-toward-85-as-wells-fargo-profit-beat-fails-to-ease-margin-concerns/). Q1 2026 fell 5.7% and Q4 2025 fell 4.61% on beats. The stock rose about 3% on the morning of these Sept 15 remarks.
findings.why_not_priced: It is only partly unpriced. The stock rose about 3% on the remarks, then fell 8.4% after the Fed hike the next day, so it now trades below its pre-conference level. Had the better margin been fully credited, WFC would not have underperformed XLF by about 4pp over the following week. The beat on the margin line lands inside 'could be better' language the company itself used in July, which limits the surprise.
findings.independence: Q2 call guidance (Mitrade transcript summary, https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1922573-20260722) is the baseline it improves on. The Hudson Labs preview still carries the older 'modest compression' framing, which suggests some previews have not updated. Same company source family as finding 3.

findings.finding: The 10-year Treasury rose from 4.44% (2026-06-30) to 5.29% (2026-09-30), about +85bp in Q3. WFC carried $250.3bn of AFS debt securities and $1,342bn of standardized RWA at June 30 with CET1 at 10.3%, inside a 10-10.5% target, and bought back $3bn in Q2. As a Category I bank its AOCI flows into CET1, so the Q3 AFS mark likely costs roughly 20-40bp of CET1, pointing to a slower Q3/Q4 buyback.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No cited instance of a WFC print turning on CET1 or buyback pace in the baseline's four prints. Q3 2025 rose 7.15% when the ROTCE target was raised, a capital and returns story.
findings.source_date: 2026-10-08 (series through); balance-sheet figures from the Q2 2026 supplement filed 2026-07-14, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/72971/000007297126000288/wfc2qer07-14x26ex992xsuppl.htm
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. WFC fell 8.4% from the 9-16 hike to 9-24 against about 4% for XLF (TIKR), which is what pricing a rate-and-capital hit looks like. The unpriced part is the reported CET1 and buyback number itself. No sell-side source found quantifies the Q3 AOCI hit, and the company has not commented on Q3 buybacks. If the market had fully priced a cut, consensus EPS would have been revised down for share count. Instead Zacks shows a marginal upward revision.
findings.independence: This is a proxy and an inference: macro-to-company transmission the company has not confirmed. The AFS hedge ratio and duration are unknown, so the CET1 hit could be much smaller. The Q2 call (Mitrade) says management is 'comfortable anywhere in' 10-10.5% and decides buybacks quarterly. TIKR (https://www.tikr.com/blog/wells-fargo-stock-is-down-14-in-2026-time-to-sell-or-load-up) independently names a Fed that keeps raising as the main risk.

findings.finding: The Fed raised rates 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, and WFC lifted its prime rate effective 09-17. 16 of 18 officials project at least one more hike in 2026. Management said in July that higher rates help ex-markets NII and hurt markets NII, and called the net effect modest for 2026. This gives a mild tilt toward the FY ~$50bn NII guide being firmed or nudged up rather than held flat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A held NII guide was the stated cause of the -2.71% on 2026-07-14, when investors had hoped for a raise. NII-guide cuts drove a -6.1% day in July 2025 (search summary of WFC's prior drops). The guide is the line with the largest observed reactions on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: The hike is public, but the stock fell on it, so the market read it as a negative (deposit costs, AOCI, credit) rather than an NII positive. If the NII benefit were priced, WFC would have outperformed, not underperformed, XLF after 9-16. The CFO's 9-15 reiteration of ~$50bn came the day before the hike and could not include it.
findings.independence: Inference only. The Q2 call (Mitrade summary) says rates are 'not a significant factor for the year' and that higher short rates reduce markets NII, which caps this finding small. FOMC outcome corroborated by https://forexfundamentals.com/economic-calendar/fomc/2026-09-16.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-14 Bank of America guided Q3 investment banking fees down at least 10% YoY, citing Dealogic data showing the IB market down about 10%. WFC's Q2 IB fees were a record $939m, +35%, so the bar for this line is high.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No WFC print in the baseline turned on IB fees. Fees are about 4% of revenue.
findings.why_not_priced: It was public a month before the print and consensus revenue ($22.15-22.34bn) was set after it, so it is largely priced. The residual is whether WFC's share gains offset the market. A 10% miss on about $0.9bn is about $90m, roughly 0.4% of revenue, which is small net of the rest of the company.
findings.independence: Contradicted in part: Jefferies' fiscal quarter to August reported record IB revenue of $1.33bn vs $1.14bn a year earlier. The window differs (Jun-Aug), but it argues against a broad slump.

findings.finding: Fed H.8 (2026-10-02 release) shows all-commercial-bank loans growing 9.0% annualized in August with C&I +19.4%, and deposits +8.1%, after Q2's +8.1% loans and +9.1% deposits. This is an independent series consistent with WFC's above-guide loan growth supporting Q3 NII.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Loan growth of 12% in Q2 did not prevent a -2.71% reaction, so balance growth alone has not been paid for.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. Management already said on 9-15 that loan growth would beat guide, and the H.8 is public. It lands inside what the company guided. What it adds is confirmation that July's soft C&I (-1.9%) reversed in August.
findings.independence: This is an industry proxy, not WFC's own number. July data were weak (loans +3.8%, C&I -1.9%), and a reclassification of $6.1bn of C&I at foreign-related institutions muddies the C&I line.

outside_window.finding: The Basel III endgame re-proposal (March 2026; about 7% lower RWA for WFC per its Q2 call) could be finalized in late 2026 and would free buyback capacity. No final rule has been found, so it is not visible inside the window.

searched_and_found_nothing: WFC 8-Ks since the Q2 print: 2026-08-19 bylaws (5.03), 2026-09-23 Scott Powell to become CRO effective 2027-01-15 (5.02), 2026-09-24 debt-issuance exhibits (9.01); none bears on Q3
No Q3 credit event tied to WFC found (the MFS UK lender exposure was February 2026 and is old news); the CFO said on 9-15 there was no delinquency deterioration
No sourced Q3 NII consensus figure
No October 2026 company-specific news or analyst preview with new information
No final Basel III rule before the print
The 2026-10-01 bank sell-off (C -4%, BAC -3%) was attributed to positioning, with no WFC-specific cause

rejected_candidates.detail: The page date is unclear and the content describes the 2022 episode. It is not a 2026 document, so it was not used.

baseline_tension: The findings are near zero net and broadly agree with the balanced skew and the -5.8% 20-day run-up. The capital negative is the part most likely already in the post-hike underperformance, and the NIM positive was paid for once (+3% on 9-15) and then given back.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sold three straight beats on NII/NIM): Q3 NIM-better finding cut from +0.5 to +0.3; it also lands partly inside the July 'could be better' language (rule 6).

Rule 5 (macro-to-company transmission unconfirmed by the company is filed small): AOCI/CET1/buyback finding cut from -0.6 to -0.5, and the rate-hike NII-guide tilt from +0.4 to +0.3; both kept, not dropped.
Rules 5 and 9 (proxy partly contradicted by Jefferies; segment about 4% of revenue): IB-fee finding cut from -0.2 to -0.15.
Rule 6 (inside what the company guided): H.8 loan-growth finding cut from +0.2 to +0.1.
Rule 7: short interest checked before the negative capital finding (0.8%, 1.72 days, not crowded), so no squeeze adjustment.
abs_move_pct (4.5) and p_up (50) unchanged; impact_sum moved from +0.30 to +0.05.
